newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Labour presses on with plan to ban tobacco ads.
newsitem.headline: Labour presses on with plan to ban tobacco ads.

text.p: Britain's newly elected Labour Party government is pressing ahead with plans to introduce a ban on tobacco advertising, its minister of state for public health told the World Health Organisation in Geneva on Wednesday.
Tessa Jowell said in a speech delivered on her behalf to the U.N. health agency's annual asembly that smoking was the biggest single cause of preventable illness and death in Britain.

"Over the coming weeks, the government will be looking at ways of introducing a ban on tobacco advertising in a bid to take concerted and effective action to reduce smoking," her speech, delivered by deputy chief medical officer Jeremy Metters, said.
Prime Minister Tony Blair has made a commitment to ban tobacco advertising in his election manifesto.

The British industry currently spends about 50 million pounds ($80 million) a year on advertising and is banned from advertising cigarettes on television and radio under a voluntary agreement, signed with the government two years ago.
The tobacco industry has called on the government to clarify its plans to ban advertising and to take into account existing restrictions under the a voluntary code.
No permanent external advertising outside shops is allowed and there are limits on total industry expenditure allowed on poster campaigns.
